Title: AKU-SONAM EA set the benchmark for faculty from Aswan University
NewsSummary: Eight nursing faculty visited AKU-SONAM in Nairobi in September from Aswan University (AU), Aswan University Hospital and the Om Habibeh Foundation. They came to learn more about classroom-based teaching in nursing education.
NewsContent:
"At SONAM, what stood out for me was the team. I like the way the team works. Most of them are highly qualified and dedicated to the place," said Dr Abdallah Mahmoud Abdallah Ali, of Aswan University Hospital as he reflected on his experience at Aga Khan University School of Nursing and Midwifery (AKU-SONAM).

Dr Abdallah was one of eight nursing faculty who visited AKU-SONAM's Nairobi campus from September 22-25, 2019. The visitors came from three institutions: Aswan University (AU), Aswan University Hospital and the Om Habibeh Foundation. The agenda was to familiarize them with classroom-based teaching in nursing education as part of the Aswan Skills Development Programme (ASDP). ASDP is a five-year initiative that features nursing faculty from AU and AKU-SONAM EA as well as support from the Aga Khan Foundation - Egypt, the Om Habibeh Foundation and Global Affairs Canada (GAC). The initiative was developed to support and equip nursing faculty at Aswan University with the capacity to deliver high-quality nursing programmes. AKU-SONAM EA's role is to facilitate curriculum development, design workshops and provide expertise in the design of clinical labs, equipment, and training for them.

Over three days, the group participated in sessions led by AKU-SONAM faculty as part of initial training in areas such as Teaching and Assessment Methodologies, Teaching with Technology, and, Establishing and Managing an Academic Library. They went through skills lab operations with Ms Beth Waweru and Ms Jane Kabo (faculty AKU-SONAM EA), toured the Aga Khan University Hospital and were involved in digital teaching and learning sessions with Mr Edward Misava (Associate, Digital Teaching and Learning Network). The last session on Establishing and Managing an Academic Library proved to be especially relevant given that the Faculty of Nursing (FoN) at AU recently received numerous books and other resources for their library provided by the Om Habibeh Foundation. Mohamed Adelatif Hussein Osman Koukobly, from the Om Habibeh Foundation, noted the importance of this session and shared that, "We have learned a lot about how to establish and manage the library. The goal of this project is to enhance the capacity of the Faculty of Nursing at Aswan University as well as to enrich how they provide services to their students, in order to develop the overall nursing profession. AKU-SONAM is providing technical assistance to help us achieve this goal."

Aswan University Hospital representatives witnessed first-hand how an effective partnership between a university and a university hospital can be realized to achieve institutional objectives during their visit to the Aga Khan University Hospital Nairobi. As Dr Abdallah shared, it's all about the team.
